subject: Cloud Computing
title: Cloud as AI's Engine Room
description: A 60-second lesson on Cloud as AI's Engine Room.

hook.text: Training GPT-4 required thousands of GPUs running for months. Without the cloud, modern AI simply wouldn't exist.

buildup.text: AI training needs massive parallel computing. Cloud providers offer GPU clusters no single company could afford to own.

discovery.text: AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud offer specialized AI chips: A100 GPUs, TPUs, and custom silicon for training and inference.

twist.text: The AI boom has created GPU shortages. Cloud GPU instances sell out months in advance. AI is straining cloud capacity.

climax.text: Cloud and AI are now inseparable. AI needs cloud scale, and cloud providers need AI workloads to fill data centers.

punchline.text: No cloud, no AI revolution. They need each other.

quiz.question: Why is the cloud essential for modern AI development?
options: AI training requires massive GPU clusters that individual companies cannot afford to own
AI algorithms can only run on cloud provider software
Cloud providers have exclusive patents on all AI technology

details.summary: Cloud computing provides the massive GPU clusters, storage systems, and networking infrastructure required to train and serve AI models. Training frontier models costs hundreds of millions of dollars in cloud compute. Without cloud scale, modern AI development would be impossible.
details.whyItMatters: AI is the biggest driver of cloud infrastructure growth. The symbiotic relationship between AI and cloud means advances in one drive demand for the other.
takeaways: Training frontier AI models requires enormous cloud GPU clusters
Cloud providers invest billions in GPU and custom AI chip capacity
AI workloads are the fastest-growing segment of cloud spending

faq.question: How much does it cost to train a large AI model?
faq.answer: Training GPT-4 reportedly cost over $100 million in compute. Frontier models from Google, Anthropic, and others require similar investments. These costs are almost entirely cloud infrastructure: thousands of GPUs running for months on high-speed interconnects.

faq.question: Why can't AI companies build their own data centers?
faq.answer: Some are starting to, but the lead time for new data centers is 18 to 24 months. Cloud providers offer immediately available GPU capacity. AI demand is volatile during research phases, making cloud's flexibility valuable. Many AI companies use both cloud and owned infrastructure.
